manifest.title: How a hot coffee cools in a room
manifest.summary: The coffee's temperature over one hour, drawn as it happens. It falls fast at first, then more slowly, and levels off at the room temperature. Change the room temperature to see the curve shift.
assumptions: Newton's law of cooling: heat loss is proportional to the coffee-room temperature difference.
Coffee starts at 90 °C; cooling constant k = 0.05 per minute (a typical uncovered mug).
Room temperature stays constant; the coffee is evenly mixed; no evaporation effects modelled separately.
manifest.description: A graph of temperature (0 to 100 °C) against time (0 to 60 minutes). A horizontal line marks the room temperature. A dot traces the coffee's temperature from 90 °C, dropping steeply at first and flattening as it nears the room line. A faint grey curve shows a 20 °C room to compare. Text on the right gives the cooling formula and notes that a bigger gap means faster cooling.
